entries: *Entry 53:

The raptors in sector 32 attempted to break out at about 10 AM this morning. Proposed solution: increase the height of the fence by 3 additional feet, and upgrade the monitoring system in that sector.

I've ordered a new shipment of fence wires, poles, and bases, as well as enough redstone to power the system. The raptors will need to be sedated while adjustments are carried out. Easier said than done.
*Entry 61:

One of the workers reported a leak in Coelacanth nursery tank number 5. Fault appears to be with the glass itself. It needs reinforced metal borders if it's going to withstand that kind of pressure long-term.
Muldoon and Harding will relocate the fish to a temporary holding pool while repairs are made. I'll add 'redesign aquatic containment' to my ever-growing list.
*Entry 69:
As our T. rex grows larger, her barrier will need reinforcement. I've designed enclosures for elephants and rhinos back at Mojang Zoo, but even those might not be enough for something this size.

Strong stone walls reinforced with a metal skeleton should hold. Top it all off with the standard redstone-powered fencing, supported by poles about 20 feet tall. That should keep her in  at least, in theory.
*Entry 74:

The Microraptors keep escaping their enclosure! Their intelligence makes them devious, and their small size and dark coloration make them nearly impossible to track. Muldoon once told me it was "like playing hide and seek with a clan of ninjas".

On top of that, they can climb and glide. So, the entire flock is being relocated to an indoor facility until their pen can be roofed and converted into a proper aviary. The only silver lining: they're not much of a threat to people.
*Entry 82:
More issues with the vehicle tour. Cars keep stopping too soon. To fix it, the redstone-powered track sections will need to be placed more frequently along the route.
If we don't get this sorted out by the end of the month, John's big showcase may have to wait. He won't like that.
*Entry 89:
The door on Feeder number 27 jammed  looks like one of the sauropods stepped on the mechanism. Another thing to fix.
Meanwhile, the raptors tried another breakout. All were sedated and returned, though one worker was injured in the process. The enclosure security is becoming a serious concern.
Also, I'm nearly out of cigarettes.
*Entry 93:
Visitors are coming this weekend. Everything needs to be fully operational no excuses. Security doors? Check. Lighting systems? Check. Containment power systems? Check. Almost there.
It feels like working for the military again, except with more teeth involved. Honestly, I miss the simpler days.
*Entry 104:
Hammond and his visitors have arrived at the park. All systems are live. This is the moment of truth  time to see if our improvements actually hold.
Hold onto your butts...
